title: Radioactive Decay and Half-Life of Fission Products
learningObjectives: Describe how half-life determines the fraction of material remaining after elapsed time
Compare decay behavior of short-lived fission products and long-lived transuranic isotopes

explanations.text: The remaining amount decreases by half for each half-life elapsed, following an exponential decay pattern described by N=N0*(1/2)^(t/T).

evidence.quote: Strontium-90 and cesium-137 have half-lives of about 30 years (half the radioactivity will decay in 30 years).

explanations.text: Isotopes decay at very different rates, with some disappearing in hours and others persisting for thousands of years.

evidence.quote: Radioactive isotopes eventually decay, or disintegrate, to harmless materials.
Some isotopes decay in hours or even minutes, but others decay very slowly.

explanations.text: Long-lived isotopes retain hazard much longer than short-lived fission products, which lose most heat and radiation after several half-lives.

evidence.quote: Plutonium-239 has a half-life of 24,000 years.
